trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line from Aeroporto station) into the city center for approximately €1.65–€2.00. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely walk through the historic Baixa-Chiado neighborhood. Explore Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square) along the Tagus River — free to visit. Stroll up Rua Augusta through the triumphal arch area and soak in the street atmosphere. Visit the free viewpoint at Miradouro de Santa Luzia in Alfama for stunning rooftop views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Alfama district, Lisbon's oldest neighborhood. Wander the narrow cobblestone streets and listen for live Fado music drifting from local tascas. Enjoy a budget dinner at a traditional tasca in Alfama.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata (custard tart, ~€1.20) and a bica (espresso, ~€0.80) at a local café near the airport or after check-in — total under €3.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bifana (pork sandwich) or prego (steak sandwich) from a local snack bar in Baixa for €2–€4.
meals.dinner: Dine at a traditional tasca in Alfama — look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, bread, and wine for €8–€12.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 24-hour Viva Viagem card for the metro/tram (€0.50 card + ~€6.40 for 24h unlimited travel) to make getting around easy on arrival day. Keep your luggage light as Alfama has steep, cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Castelo de São Jorge (St. George's Castle) — one of Lisbon's most iconic landmarks with panoramic city views. Entry is €15 for adults (book online in advance for a small discount). Arrive early to beat weekend crowds. Explore the medieval walls, towers, and archaeological site within the castle grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through Mouraria, Lisbon's oldest Moorish quarter, and into Baixa. Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience at Mercado da Ribeira — spend the afternoon grazing through the iconic food hall featuring the best local chefs and traditional Portuguese dishes. Try small plates from multiple stalls to sample a wide variety of local cuisine on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy Cais do Sodré neighborhood along the waterfront. Walk along the Ribeira das Naus promenade for free sunset views over the Tagus River. Enjoy a casual dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Café A Brasileira in Chiado or any local pastelaria — galão (milky coffee) and a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) for under €4.
meals.lunch: Time Out Market — budget €10–€15 for 2–3 small plates and a drink, choosing wisely from the more affordable stalls.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico or similar local restaurant near Cais do Sodré — grilled fish or bacalhau (salt cod) dish with house wine for €10–€14.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday can be busy at Time Out Market — go before 13:00 or after 15:00 to avoid peak lunch crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the route from the castle downhill is steep and cobblestoned.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 15E or Bus 728 to Belém (free with transport pass or ~€1.65 single). Visit the Belém Historical Monuments experience: start with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture — entry is €10 (free on Sunday mornings until 14:00, so arrive early to save money!). Then walk to the iconic Tower of Belém along the riverfront — entry is €6.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the world-famous Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) for the authentic pastel de nata — €1.40 each, eat in or take away. Explore the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) — exterior is free to admire, or pay €6 to go up for views. Walk along the riverside promenade in Belém which is beautiful and completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center via tram or bus. Head to Príncipe Real neighborhood for its relaxed, local vibe. Browse the Sunday antiques and organic market at Jardim do Príncipe Real (if still running in the evening) and enjoy the park atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a quick coffee and pastel de nata near Lisbon City Stay before heading to Belém — under €3.
meals.lunch: Pastéis de Belém for the famous custard tarts (2–3 tarts ~€4) plus a sandwich from a nearby café — total under €8.
meals.dinner: Solar dos Presuntos or a local tasca in Príncipe Real — try caldo verde (green soup) and grilled sardines or a meat dish for €10–€13 with house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday free entry to Jerónimos Monastery (before 14:00) is a major budget saver — prioritize arriving before 10:00. The Belém area is spread out but very walkable along the riverfront. Combine the Tower of Belém and Monastery visits to maximize the single tram journey.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Ancient Art (Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga) in the Lapa neighborhood — Portugal's most important art museum housing masterpieces spanning 800 years of Portuguese art, including works by Nuno Gonçalves and Hieronymus Bosch's 'Temptation of St. Anthony.' Entry is €6 (free on Sunday mornings, but today is Monday). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the permanent collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to the Chiado neighborhood for the Chiado Exploration portion of the experience. Visit the free Igreja do Carmo (Carmo Church) ruins — a hauntingly beautiful Gothic church destroyed in the 1755 earthquake, now an archaeological museum (€5 entry). Browse the Livraria Bertrand, the world's oldest operating bookshop (free to browse). Stroll through Chiado's elegant streets and squares.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bairro Alto neighborhood which comes alive in the evening. This is Lisbon's bohemian quarter with affordable bars and restaurants. Enjoy a glass of local Vinho Verde or ginjinha (cherry liqueur) at a standing bar for €1–€3.

meals.breakfast: Local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee and pastry for under €3.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Campo de Ourique (a local food market, less touristy than Time Out) — full meal for €8–€10 including a drink.
meals.dinner: Bairro Alto tasca — look for a simple menu with grilled chicken (frango grelhado) or bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) for €9–€12.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Ancient Art is closed on Mondays in some seasons — verify opening hours before visiting and swap with an afternoon Chiado exploration if needed. The Chiado area has steep hills; wear comfortable shoes. Ginjinha at the famous A Ginjinha bar near Rossio costs just €1.40 per shot — a must-try local experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market in Campo de Santa Clara (open Tuesday and Saturday mornings, free entry) — a fantastic local experience to browse vintage items, antiques, and second-hand goods. This is a great opportunity to interact with locals and pick up affordable souvenirs. Explore the nearby Igreja de São Vicente de Fora church (€5 entry, beautiful azulejo tile panels).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free ferry across the Tagus River to Cacilhas (€1.30 each way) for a completely different perspective of Lisbon's skyline. Walk along the waterfront, enjoy the views, and visit the Cristo Rei statue viewpoint area (accessible by bus from Cacilhas, entry €6). Return to Lisbon by ferry in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Lisbon — return to a favorite neighborhood for a farewell dinner. Consider revisiting Alfama for a proper sit-down Fado dinner experience at a more affordable venue, or simply enjoy a final meal in Baixa. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Feira da Ladra area — street food vendors sell fresh pastries and coffee for under €3.
meals.lunch: In Cacilhas, try a seafood restaurant along the waterfront — fresh grilled fish (peixe grelhado) with salad and bread for €10–€14, much cheaper than equivalent restaurants in central Lisbon.
meals.dinner: Final farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a traditional Portuguese meal at a Baixa restaurant. Three-course menu with wine for €15–€20 per person, or keep it budget with a final tasca meal for €10–€12.

day_by_day.notes: The Feira da Ladra flea market is only open Tuesday and Saturday mornings — this Tuesday visit is well-timed. The Cacilhas ferry is a beloved local commuter route and offers one of the best (and cheapest) views of Lisbon's skyline — highly recommended. Keep receipts for any VAT refund eligibility on purchases over €61.35 at participating shops.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate Baixa-Chiado neighborhood on foot — stroll through Praça do Comércio along the Tagus riverfront, walk up Rua Augusta through the triumphal arch, and browse the lively pedestrian streets to get your bearings in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show: Join an evening guided walking tour through Lisbon's oldest medieval neighborhood, winding through narrow alleyways, past São Jorge Castle viewpoints, and finishing with a traditional Fado performance at a local casa de fado.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack at the airport or on arrival — a pastel de nata and coffee at a café near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Chico or a neighborhood tasca near Baixa for a simple lunch plate (prato do dia) — grilled fish or bifanas for around €10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner is included as part of the Fado show experience, or dine beforehand at Zé da Mouraria for hearty, affordable Portuguese home cooking (€15–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Keep luggage light for the evening walk — wear comfortable shoes as Alfama involves steep, cobbled streets. Book the Fado show in advance as evening slots fill quickly, especially on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: National Museum of Ancient Art & Chiado Exploration: Start the morning at Portugal's most important art museum (Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga), housing 800 years of Portuguese masterpieces including the Panels of São Vicente. Allow 2 hours inside, then walk through the elegant Chiado district, browsing its bookshops, independent boutiques, and literary cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré for a leisurely afternoon grazing session. Sample dishes from Lisbon's best chefs — petiscos, fresh seafood, Alentejo cheeses, local wines, and traditional sweets — all under one roof.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chiado or Bairro Alto for the evening. Explore the lively streets as bars and restaurants come alive, and enjoy a relaxed dinner in one of the neighborhood's bistros.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café A Brasileira in Chiado — a historic café famous for its strong coffee and pastries (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Time Out Market is the lunch highlight — budget €20–25 per person for a generous spread of multiple small dishes and a glass of wine.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Rua das Flores in Chiado for modern Portuguese petiscos in a cozy setting (€25–35 per person including wine).

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Ancient Art is closed on Mondays, so visiting on Sunday is ideal. Time Out Market is busiest midday — arriving around 13:00–14:00 offers a good balance of atmosphere and availability. Chiado to Cais do Sodré is a pleasant 10-minute downhill walk.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastéis de Belém: Take Tram 15E or the riverside bus to Belém. Begin with a visit to the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a stunning example of Manueline architecture. Then walk to the iconic Tower of Belém along the Tagus riverbank.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém — visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) for panoramic views, and explore the Belém Cultural Centre area. Head back toward the city center in the late afternoon and take a leisurely walk along the Ribeira waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Lapa or Santos neighborhood, close to the Belém route, before returning to the hotel. Alternatively, head back to Bairro Alto for evening drinks and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick coffee and croissant at a local padaria before heading to Belém.
meals.lunch: The unmissable stop: Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for the original custard tarts, followed by a sit-down lunch at Solar dos Presuntos or a riverside café in Belém (€15–20).
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Ramiro (if you don't mind the trip to Intendente area) for classic Portuguese seafood — prawns, clams, and cold beer (€30–40 per person). Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery can have queues — arrive when it opens at 10:00 for the shortest wait. The Tower of Belém is small inside; the exterior and surrounding park are equally rewarding. Belém is about 6 km west of the city center — the riverside route by tram is scenic and enjoyable.

day_by_day.morning: Mouraria & Intendente Neighborhood Food & History Walk: Join a guided food and history walk through Mouraria, Lisbon's ancient Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado. Discover hidden squares, centuries-old churches, street art, and multicultural food stalls. Sample local bites along the way — from traditional petiscos to international flavors reflecting the neighborhood's diversity.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, explore nearby Martim Moniz square and the Intendente area independently. Visit the Intendente Prazeres market hall and browse the eclectic mix of shops. Walk up to the Graça viewpoint (Miradouro da Graça) for sweeping views over the city and the Tagus river.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte, Lisbon's highest and most panoramic viewpoint, ideally timed for golden hour. Then head to a local restaurant in the Graça or Mouraria neighborhood for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Mercearia do Intendente or a neighborhood café with a galão (milky coffee) and tosta mista (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Snacks and tastings are included during the Mouraria food walk. Supplement with a full meal at Taberna Sal Grosso in Mouraria for honest Portuguese cooking (€15–20).
meals.dinner: O Velho Eurico in Graça for grilled meats and fish with a local crowd in an unpretentious setting (€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Mouraria walk is best booked as a small-group guided tour for maximum historical context. Wear comfortable shoes — the neighborhood is hilly. The walk from Mouraria to Graça is uphill but manageable and very scenic. Miradouro da Graça is less crowded than Santa Catarina or Santa Luzia and offers arguably the best panorama in Lisbon.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning — revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore LX Factory, Lisbon's trendy creative hub in a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara. Browse independent shops, design studios, bookshops, and street art. On Sundays it hosts a market, but mid-week it's quieter and authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Baixa for last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up Portuguese wine, tinned fish (conservas), ceramics, or cork goods along Rua Augusta and surrounding streets. Stop at a traditional conserveira (tinned fish shop) like Conserveira de Lisboa. Enjoy a final slow afternoon coffee at a riverside café at Praça do Comércio.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a classic Lisbon restaurant to close out the trip, celebrating the best of Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or splurge on brunch at Copenhagen Coffee Lab or Café de São Bento for a leisurely start.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at LX Factory — try Cantina LX for Portuguese comfort food with a creative twist (€15–20).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa) in Chiado for an elevated but approachable Portuguese tasting experience (€45–60 per person) — a memorable final meal. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan accordingly — Lisbon Airport is 20–30 minutes from the city center by Metro or taxi. If departing on May 20, enjoy a full Day 5 without rushing. Pack tinned fish and wine carefully to comply with airline liquid and weight rules. Portugal's tap water is safe to drink — a small eco-friendly saving throughout the trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — Flight TP lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport to Lisbon City Stay hotel via private luxury transfer. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the elegant Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods near the hotel. Browse the iconic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop), window-shop at boutique Portuguese design stores, and soak in the atmosphere of one of Lisbon's most sophisticated districts. Stop at a miradouro (viewpoint) such as Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Lisbon's dining scene with dinner at Belcanto, José Avillez's two-Michelin-star flagship restaurant in Chiado, offering a contemporary Portuguese tasting menu that reimagines classic flavors with extraordinary creativity. Book the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for the full luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy complimentary breakfast or a light meal at the hotel upon arrival if hungry after the flight.
meals.lunch: Light snack or afternoon bite at A Cevicheria or Pharmácia restaurant in Chiado — vibrant, stylish, and beloved by locals.
meals.dinner: Belcanto (2 Michelin stars) — Rua Serpa Pinto 10A, Chiado. Tasting menu with wine pairing. Reservations essential and should be booked well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance for a seamless arrival. Ask the hotel concierge to confirm all upcoming experience bookings upon check-in. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Belcanto reservations must be made weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show (morning portion): Begin with a premium guided walking tour of Alfama, Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood. Wind through narrow medieval alleyways, discover hidden Moorish-era architecture, visit the Sé de Lisboa (Lisbon Cathedral), and climb to the Castelo de São Jorge for sweeping views over the terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. Your expert guide will bring centuries of history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Alfama at your own pace. Visit the National Pantheon (Igreja de Santa Engrácia) and the charming Santa Clara flea market area. Ride the historic Elétrico 28 tram through the district for an authentic local experience. Return to the hotel mid-afternoon for a rest before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Experience an intimate, premium Fado show at one of Lisbon's most respected Fado houses — Tasca do Chico or Sr. Fado — where world-class fadistas perform in an authentic, emotional setting. Dinner is served during the performance, featuring traditional Portuguese cuisine paired with excellent regional wines.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at the historic Café A Brasileira in Chiado — an iconic Art Nouveau café beloved since 1905.
meals.lunch: Taberna da Rua das Flores — a celebrated Alfama-area tavern serving refined petiscos (Portuguese tapas) using seasonal, local ingredients in an intimate setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner and Fado show at Tasca do Chico or Sr. Fado in Alfama — book the premium reserved table package for the best seats and full dinner service with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Alfama cobblestone streets. The Fado show reservation should be confirmed in advance — premium table bookings fill quickly. Bring a light layer for the evening as hilltop viewpoints can be breezy in May.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastéis de Belém: Depart by private car or taxi to the historic riverside district of Belém. Begin with a guided visit to the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture built to celebrate Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore the ornate cloisters and the tombs of Portugal's greatest explorers. Then walk to the iconic Tower of Belém, standing sentinel on the Tagus River — a symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the monuments, make the obligatory pilgrimage to Pastéis de Belém, the legendary bakery that has been producing the original pastel de nata since 1837 — a warm, flaky custard tart dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar. Afterward, visit the Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries) and stroll along the scenic Tagus riverfront promenade. Optional: visit the MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) for a contemporary cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon for a refined dinner experience. Head to the Príncipe Real neighborhood for dinner at Alma (1 Michelin star), Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's celebration of Portuguese culinary heritage with sophisticated modern technique. Follow dinner with a nightcap at a rooftop bar such as TOPO Chiado or Park Bar for stunning evening city views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a fresh galão (Portuguese latte) and pastries at a local pastelaria in Chiado before departing for Belém.
meals.lunch: Solar dos Presuntos or a riverside lunch at Taberna do Mercado near Belém — focus on fresh Atlantic seafood, grilled fish, and regional specialties.
meals.dinner: Alma Restaurant (1 Michelin star) — Rua Anchieta 15, Chiado. Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's signature tasting menu with sommelier-guided wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jerónimos Monastery tickets in advance online to skip queues. Belém is approximately 6–7 km from the city center — a private car or Uber is most comfortable. Pastéis de Belém can have queues; arrive early or be patient — it is absolutely worth it.

day_by_day.morning: National Museum of Ancient Art & Chiado Exploration: Spend a luxurious morning at the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (MNAA), Portugal's most important art museum. Housing over 800 years of Portuguese and international masterpieces — including Hieronymus Bosch's 'The Temptation of Saint Anthony' and priceless collections of gold, silver, and azulejo tiles — this is a world-class cultural experience. Arrange a private guided tour for an in-depth, exclusive visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré for a curated premium food tour. Graze through stalls helmed by some of Portugal's best chefs — sample petiscos, fresh seafood, regional cheeses, charcuterie, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and artisan pastries. This is the ultimate showcase of Lisbon's vibrant contemporary food culture in a single stunning space.
day_by_day.evening: Mouraria & Intendente Neighborhood Food & History Walk (evening edition): Join a premium guided evening walk through Mouraria, Lisbon's historic Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado. Discover hidden azulejo-tiled alleyways, ancient mosques-turned-churches, and the multicultural tapestry of this deeply historic neighborhood. End the walk with dinner at a celebrated local restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or visit Tartine bakery in Santos for exquisite fresh-baked pastries and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Time Out Market — curated tasting experience across multiple premium stalls. Budget approximately €40–60 per person for a thorough exploration including wine and dessert.
meals.dinner: Zé da Mouraria or Tasca do Chico (if not visited Day 2) — authentic, intimate restaurants in the Mouraria neighborhood serving traditional Portuguese cuisine at its most honest and flavorful.

day_by_day.notes: Book a private guide for the MNAA to get the most from the collection — the museum is vast and a knowledgeable guide transforms the experience. The Time Out Market is best visited mid-afternoon to avoid peak lunch crowds. The Mouraria walk is especially atmospheric in the early evening light.

day_by_day.morning: Optional day trip to Sintra or a relaxed final morning in Lisbon. If staying in the city, revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore the LX Factory — a creative hub in a converted 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara, filled with independent boutiques, art studios, and excellent cafés. Browse for premium Portuguese souvenirs: locally produced wine, artisan ceramics, hand-embroidered linens, or high-quality cork goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at one of Lisbon's finest restaurants. Consider Eleven (1 Michelin star) near Parque Eduardo VII, offering contemporary Portuguese-Mediterranean cuisine with panoramic views over the city and the Tagus. Afterward, take a final leisurely walk through Príncipe Real's antique markets and garden squares. Return to the hotel for packing and checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on departure flight schedule: enjoy a final sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar such as TOPO Chiado, Sky Bar at Bairro Alto Hotel, or the rooftop of Hotel de Figueira. Transfer to Lisbon Airport via private luxury car for departure, carrying memories of one of Europe's most captivating and historically rich capital cities.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — request a special spread or room service breakfast as a luxurious send-off.
meals.lunch: Eleven Restaurant (1 Michelin star) — Rua Marquês da Fronteira, Jardim Amália Rodrigues. Elegant farewell lunch with city panorama and refined Portuguese cuisine.
meals.dinner: Light farewell dinner or airport lounge dining depending on flight schedule. If time permits, tapas and wine at a Príncipe Real wine bar such as By the Wine (José Maria da Fonseca) for a final taste of Portugal.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance for departure. Allow at least 2.5 hours before international flight departure for Lisbon Airport check-in and security. LX Factory is most vibrant on Sundays with an outdoor market — if Day 5 falls on a Sunday, prioritize a morning visit. Ask the hotel concierge to store luggage after checkout if you have an evening flight.
